rawItems.title: Police investigating clash between councillors during controversial meeting
rawItems.content: Police have launched an investigation after a clash between two councillors during a controversial council meeting, it can be revealed. Cllr Stephen Ferguson clashed with Cllr Ryan Coogan at a full meeting of Huntingdonshire District Council on September 9. The incident occurred during a debate on a motion to review funds for plans to convert three cars parks into housing. Mr Coogan, the Reform councillor for Ramsey, objected after an amendment saw his motion cut from four pages to two. The pair clashed after Mr Ferguson, who chairs the district council, instructed Coogan to stop speaking and sit down. In a statement on social media shortly after the meeting, the chairman clarified his actions after "discussion online". The incident occurred during a debate on a motion to review proposals lodged by Capital and Centric (Image: Huntingdonshire District Council) "The member concerned had already spoken three times during the debate, more than any other member," he said. "At no point was I seeking to prevent them from speaking or expressing their views." Mr Ferguson claimed Mr Coogan's speech had strayed from the motion, breaching a council rule on debate. "I first tried, from the Chair, to remind the member to speak to the motion, an intervention which would have taken a few seconds," he added. "He simply continued speaking over me." Mr Ferguson said he stood during the debate, meaning the meeting had to fall silent, but Mr Coogan continued speaking over him. Read more Huntingdo
